scenario.name: Generated enterprise: Finance account compromise
scenario.description: A compromised Finance account inside a generated 120-person enterprise. Five days of ordinary working history precede the intrusion, so the account's normal devices, addresses, and applications are all observable. Nothing is pre-filtered.

actions.label: Isolate FIN-LT-004
actions.description: Cut the host off from the network while preserving it for investigation. Stops the beacon and any further lateral movement.

actions.label: Disable Yuki Lee
actions.description: Disable the compromised account in the directory so the credential cannot be reused.

actions.label: Revoke the attacker's session
actions.description: Terminate the active session established from the unfamiliar address.

actions.label: Reset the password and take no further action
actions.description: Force a password reset but leave the session and host untouched.

assessment.rationale: The established session survives a password reset, and the host continues beaconing. Containment is incomplete.

objectives.label: Compromised account disabled
objectives.description: The account used from attacker infrastructure is no longer usable.

objectives.label: Attacker session revoked
objectives.description: The session established from the unfamiliar address is terminated.

groundTruth.summary: Yuki Lee (Finance) had their account compromised from 91.219.236.18 after a short password spray. The intruder ran encoded PowerShell on FIN-LT-004, beaconed to 185.220.101.79, enumerated domain administrators, opened the restricted document payroll-export.csv, and moved laterally to FS-01 over SMB before endpoint detection fired.

timeline.significance: Failed sign-in for yuki.lee@acme.test from 91.219.236.18, an address outside every corporate subnet.

Failed sign-in for yuki.lee@acme.test from 91.219.236.18, an address outside every corporate subnet.
Successful sign-in for yuki.lee@acme.test from 91.219.236.18 minutes after repeated failures. This is the compromise point.
Interactive session established on the compromised account.
Base64-encoded PowerShell launched with an execution-policy bypass and a hidden window. No business process on this host runs this way.
Outbound connection to 185.220.101.79 on 443 immediately after the encoded command. Beaconing to attacker infrastructure.
Host and privilege discovery from the compromised session.
Domain administrator enumeration. The intruder is looking for an escalation path.
Second beacon to the same infrastructure, consistent with a callback interval.
Restricted document payroll-export.csv opened by an account that has no routine history with it. This is the business impact.
SMB connection from the compromised workstation to FS-01. Scope now extends beyond the initial host.
Endpoint detection fires on the encoded command. Everything before this is what the analyst has to reconstruct.

questions.prompt: From which source address did the successful sign-in for yuki.lee@acme.test originate?
questions.hint: Compare the account's sign-in history against the days before the incident.

questions.prompt: How many failed sign-ins from that address preceded the successful one?
questions.hint: Filter the SIEM by the source address.

questions.prompt: Which external address did the workstation beacon to after the encoded command ran?
questions.hint: Look at outbound network connections from the affected endpoint.

questions.prompt: What is the hostname of the compromised workstation?
Which restricted document did the intruder open?
questions.hint: Check file activity attributed to the compromised account.

questions.prompt: Which server did the intruder reach over SMB?
questions.hint: Destination port 445 from the affected endpoint.
